question.problem:
There are three cable TV providers in a particular apartment block: provider $A,$ provider $B,$ and provider $C.$ A study has shown that, each year

- from the tenants using provider $A,$ $80%$ swap to provider $B$ and $10%$ swap to provider $C,$

- from the tenants using provider $B,$ $25%$ swap to provider $A$ and $25%$ swap to provider $C,$

- from the tenants using provider $C,$ $70%$ swap to provider $A$ and $10%$ swap to provider $B.$

The stochastic matrix that describes this situation is given below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.1 & a & 0.7 \\ 0.8 & 0.5 & b \\ c & 0.25 & 0.2\end{aligned}]
$$

current_example.problem:
There are two groups of people in a particular city: those who use their own vehicles and those who use public transport. A study has shown that, each year

- $35\%$ of people who used their own vehicles swap to public transport, and

- $25\%$ of people who used public transport swap to their own vehicles.

Give the stochastic matrix that describes how people change their means of transportation each year.
current_example.worked_solution:
We are given the following situation for each year: - $35\%$ of people who used their own vehicles swap to public transport. This implies that $65\%$ of them remain using their own vehicles. - $25\%$ of people who used public transport swap to their own vehicles. This implies that $75\%$ of them remain using public transport. Writing this information in tabular form, we obtain the following:
From:
Vehicles Public Transport
To: Vehicles $0.65$ $0.25$
Public Transport $0.35$ $0.75$
